### What happened?

`SapConstraint<T>::MakeReduced()` replaces only the Jacobian of a constraint; the rest of the concrete constraint is cloned unchanged. Several constraints store per-clique data from construction and build their Jacobian from it:

- `SapLimitConstraint`, `SapJointFrictionConstraint`, `SapPdControllerConstraint` and `SapCouplerConstraint` store clique DOF indices and clique sizes.
- `SapTendonConstraint` stores per-clique DOF coefficient vectors.
- `SapDistanceConstraint` and `SapWeldConstraint` store their kinematics, including the Jacobian at construction.

After `MakeReduced()`, this data still describes the full problem, not the reduced one.

new_candidates.body:
**TL;DR:** on one H200, 86% of a bf16 pi0.5 chunk (133 of 154 ms) is the 10 denoise steps, which look launch-bound: `compile_model` brings the chunk to 25 ms but takes 3 to 7 minutes to warm up. Proposal: keep the prefix KV static per chunk and add an opt-in CUDA graph for the denoise step, to get most of that speedup without the compile warmup (draft PR in progress).

### Ticket Type

💡 Feature Request / Improvement

### Environment & System Info

- lerobot `main` 38b975c5b, `lerobot/pi05_base` @ 22c30e5b
- 1x H200, torch 2.11.0+cu128, transformers 5.5.4, `uv sync --locked --extra pi`

### Description

I profiled `PI05Pytorch.sample_actions` on one H200 to see where a chunk's time goes. Inputs are synthetic but shaped like `pi05_base`: 3 cameras at 224x224, 200 prompt slots (64 unmasked), chunk 50, 10 denoise steps, fixed noise. Each setting ran in its own process, 50 timed calls after 5 warmup; the first four rows ran twice in opposite order, the follow-ups once. Weights were checked tensor by tensor against the checkpoint.

| batch 1 | median ms per chunk (2 runs) | vs as shipped | first call | max abs diff vs fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp32 (as shipped) | 237 / 239 | 1.0x | 0.5 s | 0 |
| fp32 + `set_float32_matmul_precision("high")` | 148 / 149 | 1.6x | 0.4 s | 0.0003 |
| bf16 | 151 / 156 | 1.55x | 0.8 s | 0.011 |
| bf16 + `compile_model` (max-autotune) | 25.5 / 25.3 | 9.4x | 389 s cold, 46 s warm cache | 0.006 |
| bf16 + compile `reduce-overhead` (1 run) | 27.6 | 8.6x | 219 s | 0.014 vs bf16 |
| bf16 + compile `default` (1 run) | 44.2 | 5.4x | 188 s | 0.014 vs bf16 |

Where the bf16 eager time goes (CUDA events around each stage, separate runs): vision + embed 9.8 ms, prefix 12.0 ms, **10 denoise steps 133 ms** (in fp32 as shipped the prefix is 92 ms and the denoise steps 124 ms).

What that suggests:

1. **The denoise loop looks launch-bound.** Each extra denoise iteration (the step plus its Euler update) adds about 1,163 GPU ops in the profiler (10 steps minus 1 step, divided by 9), at about 13 ms per step for the `gemma_300m` expert on a 50-token suffix. Inductor alone (`default`) brings the whole chunk to 44 ms; adding CUDA graphs (`reduce-overhead`) brings it to 27.6 ms, within 9% of max-autotune.
2. **Every step copies the prefix cache.** The forward appends the suffix K/V into whatever `DynamicCache` it is given (HF Gemma updates it even with `use_cache=False`), so `denoise_step` clones the 968-token prefix cache each step and the clone grows to 1,018. Without the clone, step 2 sees 1,068 keys against a 1,018-wide mask: `The size of tensor a (1068) must match the size of tensor b (1018)`. It's the same pattern #4633 reports for SmolVLA, with a fix proposed in #4634.
3. **Compile's startup is the catch:** the first call took 188 to 420 s on a cold Inductor cache (46 s with a warm one), on top of loading the model, and a fresh machine or container pays it before its first action (#4115 is a related warmup crash in rollout).
4. **Compile at larger batch crashes:** `compile_model` at batch 8 (and with Gemma attention switched to `pi_gemma.sdpa_attention_forward`, already at batch 4) dies with `CUDA driver error: an illegal memory access`, reported at a fused cat/cumsum kernel over the 968-token prefix. Batch 4 with plain compile works (59 ms for 4 chunks), and eager bf16 at batch 8 works (240 ms).

### Context & Reproduction

Proposal, in the spirit of #4634 and #2061:

- keep the prefix K/V static once per chunk (concatenate the suffix functionally, no in-place growth, no per-step clone), and build the suffix masks and position ids once per chunk instead of every step;
- then an opt-in that captures `denoise_step` in a CUDA graph (fixed shapes per batch size and `chunk_size`), so the loop replays without `torch.compile`'s startup.

Before writing it I'd measure graph capture of the eager step on its own, since the 27.6 ms above also includes Inductor's fusion. Does this direction sound right, and is anyone already on it? Happy to open the PR.

<details><summary>How it was measured</summary>

- `sample_actions(images, img_masks, tokens, masks, noise=noise, num_steps=10)` under `torch.inference_mode()`, wall time with `torch.cuda.synchronize()`; stage times with CUDA events in separate runs so the wrappers don't touch the totals.
- bf16 arms all run at matmul precision `"high"`, the setting `compile_model` switches on, so compile isn't credited with TF32.
- "max abs diff" compares the 50x32 action chunk with the fp32 run on the same noise (the follow-up rows with bf16).
- Memory (steady state, `max_memory_allocated`): fp32 15.8 GiB, bf16 8.9 GiB, compiled 8.7 GiB.
</details>

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```
RuntimeError: CUDA driver error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  ... torch/_inductor/cudagraph_trees.py ... run_eager
  ... triton_spl_fused__to_copy_cat_cumsum_expand_sub_unsqueeze_22.run(..., 4, 968, ...)
```
(batch 4 with SDPA attention; batch 8 plain compile fails the same way)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

For anyone hitting the latency today: `dtype: bfloat16` plus `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")` is ~1.55x with no compile warmup; `compile_model` is ~9x if a few minutes of first-call compile is acceptable.

new_candidates.body:
The replacement RTX pipeline still assumes the first OVRTX output frame is the camera capture. Investigate the native multi-frame contract before choosing a fix.

At current main `90a16f06685dbf7948262eafa628c470b4cdc78c`:

- [`OVRTXRenderer._process_render_products`](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/90a16f06685dbf7948262eafa628c470b4cdc78c/source/isaaclab_ov/isaaclab_ov/renderers/ovrtx_renderer.py#L921-L943) selects `product.frames[0]` and ignores additional frames.
- [`CameraCfg.render_settings`](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/90a16f06685dbf7948262eafa628c470b4cdc78c/source/isaaclab/isaaclab/sensors/camera/camera_cfg.py#L100-L105) supports per-product attributes, [authored directly onto the product](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/90a16f06685dbf7948262eafa628c470b4cdc78c/source/isaaclab_ov/isaaclab_ov/renderers/ovrtx_usd.py#L236-L243), including `omni:rtx:dlss:frameGeneration`.
- Pinned [OVRTX v0.6.0 frame timing documentation](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovrtx/blob/b9ae5f0913847502ff5ed29ab45a6e9f28bec8f1/python/ovrtx/_src/types.py#L873-L897) permits multiple DLSS-G outputs and distinguishes interpolated frame capture times from the real frame. It does not explicitly guarantee list ordering.

If an intermediate image is first, IsaacLab publishes it and ignores the real/current capture. A lightweight reproduction executing the unchanged current-main selection method with synthetic frames produced:

```text
single real frame: selected=real/current, capture_time=1.0, ignored=0
chronological multi-frame output: selected=generated/intermediate, capture_time=0.5, ignored=1
```

This confirms selection behavior for that input, not native OVRTX frame ordering. No native DLSS benchmark was run: the installed OVRTX version differs from the pinned runtime, and dependencies were left unchanged.

## Investigation and acceptance criteria

- On the pinned OVRTX runtime and supported hardware, record returned frame counts, capture times, ordering, and AOV keys with frame generation enabled.
- Define the single-frame sensor contract and explicitly select the intended real/current capture. Use list position only if the SDK guarantees its meaning.
- Preserve matching asynchronous capture metadata and PPISP inputs.
- Extend the [existing renderer contract coverage](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/90a16f06685dbf7948262eafa628c470b4cdc78c/source/isaaclab_ov/test/test_ovrtx_renderer_contract.py#L302-L310), which supplies one frame per product, with distinguishable intermediate/real outputs and capture times. Assert published pixels and matching metadata, and demonstrate fail-before/pass-after.
- Preserve ordinary single-frame behavior.

The current RTX visualizer [displays sensor pixels in a Newton GL window](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/90a16f06685dbf7948262eafa628c470b4cdc78c/source/isaaclab_visualizers/isaaclab_visualizers/newton/newton_visualizer.py#L733-L739). Presenting every generated frame at an increased cadence requires separate presentation work; repeatedly overwriting one camera buffer would not achieve it.

Related: #8583, closed as superseded by the adapter removal in #8585. This issue tracks the remaining question against the active architecture.
new_candidates.title: Investigate OVRTX sensor frame selection when DLSS frame generation returns multiple frames
